questions.question: Term for an error or defect in a program.
questions.explanation: Bugs make software behave incorrectly; 'debugging' means fixing them.

questions.question: Small update that fixes bugs or security flaws in software.
questions.explanation: Patches are minor fixes released between major versions.

questions.question: A copy of data kept for recovery after loss or damage.
questions.explanation: Backups let you restore files after deletion, failure, or ransomware.

questions.question: Term for transferring data from a remote server to your device.
questions.explanation: Downloading pulls data — like files or streams — to your device.

questions.question: Term for sending data from your device to a remote server.
questions.explanation: Uploading pushes data out, such as posting photos or backing up files.

questions.question: General term for malicious software like viruses and spyware.
questions.explanation: Malware is any software designed to harm or exploit a system.

questions.question: Temporary storage that speeds up access to recently used data.
questions.explanation: Caches keep frequently used data close at hand in browsers, CPUs, and apps.

questions.question: Clickable text or image that opens another page or file.
questions.explanation: Hyperlinks connect web pages; clicking one navigates to its target.

questions.question: Saved shortcut to a web page inside a browser.
questions.explanation: Bookmarks (or favorites) store page addresses for quick return.

questions.question: A small window that appears on top of the page, often an ad.
questions.explanation: Pop-ups open over content; browsers include pop-up blockers.

questions.question: The smallest single dot that makes up a screen image.
questions.explanation: Pixels are the tiny colored dots forming every display image.

questions.question: Temporary holding area for cut or copied data.
questions.explanation: The clipboard stores your last cut or copy until you paste.

questions.question: On-screen indicator showing the mouse position or text insertion point.
questions.explanation: The cursor shows where mouse clicks or typed characters will land.

questions.question: Secret word or phrase used to log in to an account.
questions.explanation: Passwords authenticate users; long unique passphrases are strongest.

questions.question: A captured image of what is shown on the screen.
questions.explanation: Screenshots save the current display as an image for sharing or records.
